source.topic: why the viral 'kill every mosquito' bucket trap doesn't actually work, and what UF entomologists say genuinely reduces yard mosquitoes
source.angle: the HONEST version of the niche's biggest format (KILL EVERY Mosquito The [old] Way - Elias Yoder's original did 25,764 views/day, 1.99M views). Instead of cloning the overclaim, Walt tells the truth UF's own extension publishes: no single trap is a magic bullet ('like trying to capture all the grains of sand on the beach' - Jonathan Day, UF entomologist), and the actually-effective old-fashioned method is source reduction (eliminating standing water), which UF/IFAS calls 'the most important technique that homeowners can employ.'
source.research_note: tools/yt_research.py --niche home-hacks: 'KILL EVERY [pest] The AMISH Way' dominates all 3 windows (24h/30d/365d); Elias Yoder original 25,764 v/d, Arrow Pest Service 24,518 v/d, and clones are STILL gaining fresh traction this month (36/d, 20/d, 9/d on videos <30 days old) - demand hasn't cooled. tools/validate_topic.py run twice: broad phrase 'natural mosquito trap that actually works without chemicals' -> NO-DEMAND (wrong phrasing, doesn't self-suggest); narrower 'natural ways to get rid of mosquitoes' -> GO-NARROW (8/12, LOW confidence due to query drift, freshness reads as cooling 0.1x on the drift-affected sample but real comps in the exact matching format run 17-25min and are still fresh). User confirmed proceeding despite the mixed/low-confidence signal, citing the strong historical winnability (21x-312x small-channel breakouts exist in this search space) as the stronger prior. Full evidence in conversation transcript 2026-08-04.
